text:
Macklin Celebrini's numbers this season look a notch below last year's 115 points, and the gap is mostly the puck not going in. He's shooting 10.2%, under the bottom of our range for him, and his nine goals trail his 10.15 expected goals (the quality of his chances). Over his last ten games he has 12 points against 14.1 expected. The process is all there: 88 shots, 23 minutes a night, and the Sharks are far better with him on the ice than without him.

The weekend suggested the bounces are turning. A line with Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg has taken off since it was put together, combining for eight points in Sunday's win over Nashville, and Daily Faceoff ran the headline "Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith finally back to normal for Sharks." Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 12.8 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among forwards, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 12th among forwards in wins above replacement. At 20, he's the engine, and a shooting rate this low is the kind that usually corrects.
